text_fidelity_a:
New Balance Dual Hydration Pack - Two 10 oz. Water Bottles with Adjustable Belt and Zippered Pockets - Reflective Details for Visibility - Water Pack for Running, Walking, Jogging, and Camping I got this for short hikes when I need to bring water and a few items but not deal with the backpack. It works great! I can fit my iphone, ID, and keys in the pouch along with a powerbar or energy gel pack. Note, though, that I have an iPhone SE so it's not huge - larger ones may not fit too well. There's a zipper pouch with a pocket inside and a thin outer pocket with a velcro closure. The velcro is pretty strong, but if you need easy access to an energy bar or gel, you could put it in there. Personally I use that one for any garbage (gel/bar wrappers) to toss out properly when I get back home. (also good to have a little T.P. and ziplock baggie along for bathroom emergencies - put the used T.P. in the ziplock and dispose properly when you get home - leave no trace! :) )

The 2- 10oz water bottles are good and easy to access. I like that the holders they go in have elastic to keep them snug and in place. I'm not sure how these would do for running as I've only used this for hiking so far. But I don't think they'd fall out while running - at least not at the pace I would go! The belt it comfortable and easy to adjust. I can size it to fit me (I'm a women's size 2) or my hubby (32" waist) quite easily.

There are those extra elastic loop things on the belt where you can clip things to it, like maybe a hat or - I don't know what. Have not used them, but could come in handy some day.
text_fidelity_b: New Balance Dual Hydration Pack - Two 10 oz. Water Bottles with Adjustable Belt and Zippered Pockets - Reflective Details for Visibility - Water Pack for Running, Walking, Jogging, and Camping

ABSOAR Cycling Bike Lights Front and Rear Silicone LED Water Resistant Headlights Tail Light High Intensity for Safety, 2 Pack Most headlights have a lens that casts forward, to amplify the LED(s) so that you can brightly see what is in front of you. This lens arrangement offers little-to-no side exposure to alert side drivers of your presence.

These lights are visible from the front or back (depending on your placement) PLUS from the sides.

I bicycle with four lights, solid and strobing white lights in the front and solid and strobing red lights in the back. Each of the front and back light has side strobe exposure.

I also wear a neon yellow reflective vest and drivers still turn right into me. I know to brake hard at a moment's notice and that knowledge has probably saved me an injury at least a few times.

After I brake hard and raise my hands in the air to say "WTF," the driver says, "I DIDN'T SEE YOU." Me, with all this regalia of lights and reflective strips on my vest, "Seriously?"

Drivers just don't think. They just turn the wheel and apply pressure to the foot controls.

Just do the best you can and make certain that you have side light coverage.
text_fidelity_b: ABSOAR Cycling Bike Lights Front and Rear Silicone LED Water Resistant Headlights Tail Light High Intensity for Safety, 2 Pack

Sunny Health & Fitness Premium Treadmill Features Auto Incline, Dedicated Speed Buttons, Bluetooth Connectivity, Built-In Speakers, Digital Performance Display and Pulse Sensors - SF-T7515 This is a solid purchase for the price. It is relatively easy to assemble (some of the pieces didn't line up correctly and required some manhandling to make it work), it is easy to use, and it feels solid. The thing I truly love is the auto incline adjustment. I can't imagine having to do that manually.

Main issue is the sound system. Terrible to say the least. Speakers buzz unless you adjust cord just right (and then the vibration from running will get it out of whack again). The sound controls on the treadmill do not work, and the sound is generally bad. For me, not a deal-breaker. Just disappointing. Also, there is an occasional squeaking in the treadmill that is irritating but, again, not a problem so far. One thing to be aware of, though. The track is narrow. It is fine for me and my daughter, but my husband hits the sides pretty regularly.

Like I said, fine for the price. But all three of agree that next purchase will be a big upgrade. We wanted to test the treadmill-use waters, and this was a great first purchase.

For many exercises, like a dumbbell shrug or a dumbbell step-up, I am using fairly heavy weights - e.g., 40 pounds or more in each hand. It had gotten to the point where my grip strength was not sufficient to hold these dumbbells comfortably while working out. I thought these hooks would be a good way to distribute the weight. -Stainless steel construction will last forever

text_fidelity_a:
Sit N Cycle sitNcycle SNC2 Dorothy Hamill Deluxe XL Low Resistance Exercise Bike This is a low resistance exercise bike. The design is surprisingly solid, with one major problem: the belts are the wrong size!

This is why most people have torn belts in these things. Belt replacement is a major repair, requiring box/socket wrenches and allens, belt routing and careful tension adjustment and alignment.

The good news is that I figured out what belts do work in this thing:
4PJ610 (the wide belt, this is the same as OEM)
3PJ610 (the narrow belt, this is longer than OEM which was 3PJ584).
You can buy belts from Ametric, that's the only place I found.

You could probably get a shorter wide belt instead, but the combination above works pretty well - if tightened sufficiently, there is quite a bit of resistance in this bike.

The reason you want a longer narrow belt is because the tension adjustment is done on both belts at the same time, and the narrow belt is then overtightened and soon rips. Hope this helps you.

I also discarded all the plastic body parts, it's a naked bike now. After taking this thing apart twice, you'll want to do the same...

I sit on this bike when I work at my height-adjustable desk, sometimes all day.
text_fidelity_b: Sit N Cycle sitNcycle SNC2 Dorothy Hamill Deluxe XL Low Resistance Exercise Bike

The first 4 nights it was a bit softer in the morning than it was when I went to bed the previous night, but it was acceptable. On the 5th night I woke up in a taco: I was laying almost on the floor with the sides of the bed puffed up on either side of me.

This thing does have some nice features. I really like that there's a compartment for the cord. I like that the motor can deflate as well as inflate the bed. And the non-slip covering is very nice. I was surprised at how well the sheets stayed on the bed, especially since there's not much for a deep fitted sheet to grab on to, and literally nowhere to tuck in a flat sheet. (My flat sheet was just long enough to tuck under the whole bed, but since the bed is >2' high when inflated, that may have been luck.)

But it doesn't matter how fabulous the features are. If it completely deflates after only a few nights of use, it's a bad bed.I returned it. Guess I'll stick with AeroBed.

JumpSport Heavy Duty Durable Trampoline Anchor Safety and Stability Kit Set Includes 4 Screws and Straps for High Winds A great product. Last winter we lost a much beloved trampoline to extreme winds. I set out on a search for a product that could prevent the loss of the replacement trampoline. I found a number of products on various websites that could best be described as variations on a tent stake design. They offered stakes that were straight or U shaped, and I was very nervous that in a windy situation (especially with rain softened ground), that the stakes would just pull free. I was about to fashion my own solution using spiral dog stakes when I found this kit.

Suffice it to say that the components are sturdy and well made. They are packaged well, and the instructions are clear and easy to follow. However, what makes this a five star product is that it contains everything you need to create a stable tie down for a trampoline, and it contains enough anchors to tie it down for wind from any direction. The anchors are not trivial to "screw" into the ground. I did it on a day after heavy rains and still required a tool for leverage. This was reassuring, because it meant that they would hold fast when the ground dried, and would allow the straps to transfer load from the trampoline frame to the stakes and the ground effectively.

I was very pleased with the product, and would heartily recommend it.

UPDATE: This stakedown kit works very well. Since installing, we have had four windstorms with gusts over 20 mph, and the trampoline has stayed perfectly in place. Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: JumpSport Heavy Duty Durable Trampoline Anchor Safety and Stability Kit Set Includes 4 Screws and Straps for High Winds

text_fidelity_a:
Kryptonite Evolution LITE Mini-6 11mm U-Lock Bicycle Lock , Black This lock is exactly what I need, but the lock I received from Amazon today had a cylinder that operates very difficultly. Kryptonite says the lock is a new design, and I wonder if they have all the bugs out yet. At one point the key would only go in half-way and I could see that the back layers of the cylinder were out of line with the outer layers. I don't know how many layers there are, but since the key would only go in half-way there was no way to turn the back layers so they would line up with the outer layers. Finally, after turning the key back and forth very gently for about ten minutes the layers lined up and the key would go in all the way. Unfortunately, the key continued to meet resistance as it turned in the cylinder and I had to ask Amazon for a replacement.

I would not trust the lock I received to operate properly away from home. I have several other Kryptonite locks and the keys all turn very freely in the cylinders. I wonder if I got a bad lock or if Kryptonite is going to have problems with this new design.

Update:

Looking at the lock further, I realized the black housing that rotates to cover the keyhole was also operating very difficultly. As I tuned the housing I saw fibrous plastic shavings visible under the edge of the housing around the keyhole. I removed several shavings with tweezers, and as I turned the cover back and forth more shavings worked their way out around the keyhole. As I pulled them out the keyhole cover began to rotate more easily. All of the shavings in the attached photo came from under the keyhole cover of the lock! If any of the shavings found their way down into the cylinder while the lock was being assembled, or when it was bounced around during shipping, that could explain why the cylinder is difficult to turn and the layers of the cylinder sometimes get out of line with each other as the key is inserted or removed from the lock.

Further Update:

Today, while waiting for Amazon's replacement lock to arrive, I looked again at the lock. Looking at the keyhole with a strong flashlight it appears the design of the metal body of the lock includes a narrow split that extends from the keyhole toward the black plastic end of the lock. I can't see how far the split extends, but I can guess that if it has sharp edges, and if the rotating black keyhole cover is shaped too tightly around the lock body, or if the keyhole cover has an uneven underside, the action of rotating the cover back and forth to uncover and recover the keyhole could actually cause the sharp edges of the split in the lock body to make the shavings I found. If any of the shavings work their way into the cylinder that, in turn, could cause the difficult cylinder operation I encountered.

Final Update:

One comment asked if the replacement lock had the same problem - it did not! I am happy with the replacement lock and so far it has worked fine.
text_fidelity_b: Kryptonite Evolution LITE Mini-6 11mm U-Lock Bicycle Lock , Black

text_fidelity_a:
HOPSOOKEN 30L Ultra Lightweight Travel Water Resistant Packable Backpack for Hiking Cycling Sports Daypack Backpack/Ultralight and Handy (Black New) This is a lightweight (in all aspects) bag that is great for limited purposes. It is made out of extremely thin and flexible material. It can fold up into itself and zip up (see picture) for easy storage and transport when not using it to carry items in. I can see this bag as being an excellent option for travelers who might find themselves needing another bag/storage option at the last minute. Like when you realize at the airport your bag is overweight and to avoid a huge baggage fee, you wish you had a small bag you could put some heavy items in and carry it on the plane instead. This would be perfect for that. Or you spend the holidays with relatives and they send you home with more goodies for the kids than you have room in your luggage for.

It's not a primary use bag. There is no padding at all. Not in the bottom of the bag. Not in the shoulder straps. There is no protection for items within the bag or your shoulders. It would not be comfortable carrying this with anything substantial or heavy inside. The material reminds me of an inexpensive windbreaker or poncho.

Pros:
Great backup bag for unexpected situations
Lightweight and very compact
Folds and zips into itself for easy storage and transport

Cons:
Flimsy shoulder straps with no padding
Questionable ability to carry heavy, rigid items like books or glass bottles
No padding in the bag itself, thus no protection for items inside

I received this bag for minimal cost in exchange for my unbiased review.
text_fidelity_b: HOPSOOKEN 30L Ultra Lightweight Travel Water Resistant Packable Backpack for Hiking Cycling Sports Daypack Backpack/Ultralight and Handy (Black New)

Luckily I dropped this pump in my cycling jersey pocket on the way out.  I had no problem getting a good seal between the pump and presta valve-thumbs up  on the hose versus other pumps with just the head-I pumped in series of 25.  After a while the tire( 700x25) felt pretty full,  was not too strenuous.  I did not want to risk blowing the new tube by over inflating.  So I finished the last 10 miles on my ride.  I checked the pressure with my floor pump and I had 80 PSI-I normally run 110- in the tire.  Not optimum, but it got me home safely, within tire specs,  and beats walking!!  My only ding of this product is no pressure gauge on the pump.  Overall if you need a small pump that can fit in your cycling jersey that can get you to a respectable road bike tire pressure relatively easily, and does not require swapping parts out for Presta and Schradervalves,  this is the pump!

text_fidelity_a:
Rhino Laces Unbreakable Shoe Laces, Reflective Black, Medium These are impressive laces. They are stiff, strong and can be pulled tight. I have been using two new pairs in mid and full size hiking boots that were a little large and I wanted them too fit snugly. They are working fine except for the length (longer than should be for the boots) and the bows can slip. I have been experimenting with tightening and using double knots. Each pair came with a different cord lock The metal one designed by Rhino so far seem too complicated to use and is time consuming setting it up. The plastic ones already broke. So, I like the laces and they are working the way I expected. I do need to master a better way to tie them.

1/5/15-After using these laces (two pairs on high and low hiking shoes), or trying to use these laces for 6 weeksI have given up and replaced them with waxed hiking laces. As noted, the two different style cord locks that were sent with each pair of laces didn't work, I then bought two other styles of cord locks, which were useless. As a result I had to continue to double knotting them, which prevented slippage and untying but due to the stiffness (like wires) I had to repeat the tying process several times, which was time consuming, and because of the stiffness of the laces, couldn't tie them tight-in fact that were always loose.

Basically, these laces will work for someone that is concerned about exposure to fire-I was not. I bought them because I try and support Kickstarter products and assumed that they would work. They did not for me. Over time the laces develop kinks, like wires and this memory remains. The result s very frustrating if you knot them, as I did.

I assume that they would work as intended with an appropriate cord lock, which I gather the inventor of the laces is trying to develop.
text_fidelity_b: Rhino Laces Unbreakable Shoe Laces, Reflective Black, Medium

TRX All-in-One Suspension Training System: Weight Training, Cardio, Cross Training, Resistance Training. Full Body Workouts for Home, Travel, and Outdoors. Includes Indoor & Outdoor Anchor system The physical therapist at the hospital had me work on hers when I came in. She thinks the TRX system is the bee's knees. When the thearopy was over I bought one.

Importantly note that the physical therapist specifically told me not to get a knock off unless it had a single strap. If the straps were not connected I would lose the balance building part and she said it would hurt me more than help. The TRX was the only one I saw, at the time, that met her criteria.

I love working on it. In my opinion, There are a couple of things to consider. First is that at my age and inflexibility, the lower body work outs are difficult. You have to get your feet in the straps a certain way and sometimes I find it hard to keep the feet in and do the workout.

The next consideration is that it is difficult to use in a closed door. You really need a fair amount of space around you to work out, and I find a closed door is a hindrance.

Overall i must grudgingly admit the physical therapist is right and the TRX system is just about perfect for getting that resistance training which is so important.
text_fidelity_b: TRX All-in-One Suspension Training System: Weight Training, Cardio, Cross Training, Resistance Training. Full Body Workouts for Home, Travel, and Outdoors. Includes Indoor & Outdoor Anchor system

SEE THE PICTURES I JUST TOOK, 2 from the outside (left and right sides) and two from the inside (left and right). After the first 10 minutes, I saw that the charcoal on the top was still completely black with no signs of the flame touching them.  Just then, I saw a very strange chemical-type reaction occurring on the outside of the canister!  It was as if a magic invisible paintbrush with white paint on it was stroking heavy stripes of paint around the outside of it!  We were shocked to see this odd thing happening!  About 15 minutes later, We finally saw small flames inside that were approaching the top briquettes.  As soon as we saw the top ones beginning to get a little grey color, we emptied it out, and the whole process took 30 minutes -- not the 15-20 we were expecting.  After we poured in the briquettes, which were already fully completely white and falling apart at the bottom, we began to cook with what remained in the canister.  I don't think this thing was operating properly at all, and I knew something was wrong when I saw this horrible discoloration happening only 10 minutes into the process.  I feel like this was made with some cheap foreign material and am very upset that my new chimney starter was ruined and unable to perform on DAY ONE.  I don't even think this thing is safe, because if it's being compromised in this way and the metal is underperforming, who knows what's going to happen to the metal on SUBSEQUENT uses, the metal and the bolts that is supposedly holding the handle onto the canister?? text_fidelity_a:
Trek Tents 10 x 14' Canvas Cabin Tent Khaki Yes, it Does work. Tension is the key.
Looking at the pictures of this tent you can see that it Should work, but you Doubt it, right??
Here on the NorthCoast of California right next to that big body of water, we have normal breezes running around 15 mph. When it gets a bit Windy it'll run around 35 mph. Then there's when it gets brisk ;>
It's still hanging out in the place I'd staked it when other tents had hopped the fence and wandered down the street.
I'd gotten tired of having to replace those nylon things every year or two and wanted something a lot more permanent in a temporary structure.
The canvas is IT for me!
I like that they'd used a white for the roofing giving you a more open feeling than you'd have otherwise if they'd gone with the base color.
I'm very happy with the construction. Tabs, zipper-pulls, netting in doors and windows. The floor is sturdy enough to dance on.
The tie-downs and stakes need to be replaced. I'm really very disappointed that this tent has such a poor finish after all the fine work they'd done for the main structure.
The skinny and very stretchy nylon strings and skinny smooth metal pins they give you stretch when dampened and the pegs pull out. It's an easy fix, not to worry. Just get a length of REAL Rope and re-do the tie-downs and buy a handful of those lovely orange plastic pegs that have teeths and you'll Keep the proper tension in the roof you need for when you get 3 inches of rain dumped on you, even With the rain-fly covering the roof. You will of course need to re-adjust the tie-downs after this happens. Good News!! Even with a couple of tub fulls of rain on the tent that you'll need to dump off, the tent Remains STANDING!

UPDATE:
After the ground got SUPER saturated with days of rain and some SERIOUS winds and GUSTS, it's collapsed Twice and the rain fly has completely died. The tie down banding along one edge RIPPED OFF and the ties From the tent to the Center pole ripped off.
The rain fly needs to be anchored SEPARATELY if you also have issue with winds. Since it's integrated with the tent, it causes Severe wall flapping and even with heavy duty metal tent pegs doing their Best, it still collapses.
NOT A HAPPY CAMPER :(((
2ND UPDATE:
We have some fairly Serious WIND and RAIN issues here and this tent does NOT hold up. The first thing that went was the rain fly, as you might have noted from my First post.
I'd replaced the useless tie down strings that came with and got some screw in the ground pegs to hold the metal framing, also noted above.
Now, the loops are ripping out.
I'D RETURN THIS TENT IF I COULD. Not sure what I'm going to do with a $600 bit of canvas that I CANNOT USE AS A TENT :(((
(too bad the vendor doesn't monitor these reviews)
text_fidelity_b: Trek Tents 10 x 14' Canvas Cabin Tent Khaki

text_fidelity_a:
Pflueger Patriarch LP Baitcast Reel, 20-Pound Max Drag I'm loving this reel. It replaced an Ambassadeur 5500C. The differences are pretty obvious. The Patriarch includes both a friction and magnetic breaking system. This might be a good thing if you have experience but it does take some time to get used to it. Nearest I can figure, the magnetic breaking is most effective at the beginning of the case where the speed is highest while the mechanical brake operates across the whole cast. When I change lures I usually turn up the magnetic to 8-10 and then adjust the mechanical until I clean casts. Then I back off the magnetic for the same result. The end result is nice long casts with fewer rats nests. Then - to add to the complication - you can pop off the side and adjust how many magnets are active in the magnetic breaking. I keep two on and four off (must be done in pairs). I get a few more yards (5 to 10 maybe) from the Patriarch compared with the 5500c.

Reeling back in is smooth. The moving eye lays the line smoothly on the spool but I notice that during casting the eye stays in one place. I can't remember for sure but I thought the 5500c eye moved during casts. Careful when you release the spool. The tension on the line may be enough to get the spools spinning and you can end up with a rats nest without even casting.

The Patriarch fits nicely in the palm while on the rod. It allows me to keep a finger on the spool and keep in touch with the line out the front. I have it mated to a St. Croix Legend Tournament Bass Casting Rod and I think the combination is perfect though I'd like to try it out with a slightly lighter and slower action rod. I'll bet it can shoot a 1/2 ounce lure a half mile!

I didn't like my dealings with support. As I mentioned, you can engage or disengage magnets in the break system but I couldn't figure out how. The minimal instruction pamphlet didn't give any clues and neither did their support website. In fact, looking through some forums I'm guessing most people find access to the magnets obvious. But I didn't know how to do it and support responded with "Unfortunately, to experiment with the centrifugal breaks, you must take
the reel apart to access them." Wow. Helpful guys. Maybe I lost something in the translation. I don't know. Fortunately for me I feel the reel is so well built I'll never have to contact support so I'll just ignore them.

You can fish well with any nice baitcaster. This isn't going to put bigger or more fish on your hook. But you'll find each cast is a pleasure.
text_fidelity_b: Pflueger Patriarch LP Baitcast Reel, 20-Pound Max Drag

text_fidelity_a:
Ringside Gel Boxing MMA Hand Wraps Once in a while a product comes along that looks like it might pose a solution to a different problem than what it is actually intended for. These Ringside Gel Wraps are obviously designed to protect your hands while either working out or sparring in the ring. But I ordered them for a different unrelated purpose -- protecting my knuckles while cutting/trimming trees in our wetlands. We live in Southwest Florida where the brush grows all year around and not only grows quickly but also tries to choke out its neighbors by fighting for the available sunlight and water. That makes for tight quarters and a lot of "barked" knuckles while maneuvering tools and changing positions.

There are pros and cons to how this product is constructed:

PROS
1. They fit your hands ergonomically without limiting your flexibility. I am actually typing this review with the gloves on.
2. The gel padding on the knuckles is positioned for proper protection and provides a feeling of confidence and security.
3. There is a stretchy strap just below the knuckles that helps keep the glove in position.
4. The glove fastens around your wrist with an adjustable velcro strap.
5. There is a second strap that fastens over the first one which holds the velcro strap in place and actually provides good wrist support.
6. The gloves are breathable and machine washable.
7. Last but not least, they come in several colors: blue, grey, pink, and red.

CONS
1. Even though I am a bigger guy, I have always worn a large size in every type of glove. Be warned that these gloves run small.
2. While the overall construction is quite good, the sewing around the cut-off fingers is not uniform. The point where the gloves are
cut off (on the inside of the hand) are folded under and stitched together -- at least that was the intention. However the stitching is
"balled up" in different parts and loose strings are evident in some of the fingers. That appears to be a quality control problem.
3. I am assuming that since the gloves are too small for me that the smaller size carries over to make the fingers too tight for comfort.
Perhaps that will loosen up with wear and washing.

So overall I think that this is a great product for what it is intended, but at 65 years old I'm not the guy to punch someone with them on or
to test them out in any manner that would hurt these old bones. At my age I'm trying to protect myself, not break my hands. The manufacturer might want to take a closer look at how the fingers are sewn together, but overall this is a good looking product that should serve its purpose quite well.
text_fidelity_b: Ringside Gel Boxing MMA Hand Wraps

text_fidelity_a:
Coast DX355 Double Lock Folding Knife I've been looking for a folding knife that I could use around the farm. This knife is 4.5 inches long and 1.5 inches wide when folded, so it has a nice sized blade while still being small enough not to get in my way when clipped onto my pocket. (There is a strong, nearly 3-inch-long metal clip securely screwed into the knife handle.) The entire knife appears to be made out of a sturdy, stainless steel. The handle has a texture and finger indentations to assure a secure grip when used.

I've never used a folding knife with a locking mechanism, but I expected at least some advertising pointing out how the special double-locking mechanism works. There wasn't any information included with the knife, but it was fairly easy to figure out. The linear lock is beneath the blade and automatically locks when the blade is fully extended. The safety switch is a toggle on the handle behind the blade. You can push it up when the blade is open to prevent the linear lock from being depressed (which would allow the blade to close). To close the blade, push the toggle back to the original position and depress the linear lock while folding the blade. Once I figured it out, it was easy to do.

Since it's winter, I haven't had much time to test the blade out for how well it keeps it edge or other wear issues. I'll post an update is anything significant comes up.
text_fidelity_b: Coast DX355 Double Lock Folding Knife

It’s quite simple to operate in that it has a single pushbutton that, on the first push, puts it in low mode, second push puts it in high mode, and third push turns it off. The low mode is a quite substantial amount of light in itself, and high mode is a very bright light. The flashlight feels quite nice in the hand. Installing the battery is quite simple as well. You simply put the battery in the back of the flashlight body and twist to align two white dots. The package comes with a USB type-C connector cord for charging. The battery itself has an input for the type-C connector for charging and a standard USB output port that can be used to charge other devices, which is a really cool feature. I like that this rechargeable battery doesn’t need product-specific charger. There is a three light battery charge level indicator on the back of the battery that is operated with a small push button. When the button is held for 2+ seconds, a small LED light comes on, giving you a light on the battery even if when not attached to the flashlight. Again, a really cool feature. Warranty on the battery and the flashlight is 3 years. The battery is part of a multi-product system that utilizes the same battery type for all devices. I really don’t find anything about this flashlight system that I don’t like. I think they have a winner here.  Made in China
text_fidelity_b: Coleman OneSource Rechargeable Camping System

text_fidelity_a:
Bike Hoist Bicycle Lift for Garage Ceiling Storage, Heavy Duty Mountain Bicycle Hanging Rack with 3 Pulley and 45 ft Adjustable Rope | 100 lb Capacity You could assemble the components for a better bike hoisting system at any decent hardware store, but the part you would buy would cost two or three times as much, and you would spend a fair amount of time figuring out what to buy and how to assemble it.

I see several review that report the packaging indicates a lesser weight capacity than the 100 lb indicated in the listing. My packaging shows the weight capacity as 45 kg -- 100 lb. Regardless, I am confident that, in fact, much more than 100 lb. could be supported by this hardware. The actual limiting factor on weight capacity will not be the hardware provided, but rather the installation method. The box includes screws with plastic anchors that are normally used for installing screws in sheetrock. Anyone who uses those to attach to a sheetrock ceiling will almost certainly have a problem. Even if the plastic anchors are used to attach the hardware to wood trusses the result will be weaker than if screwed directly into the wood after a proper size hole has been pre-drilled. Other reviews contain suggestions for mounting. The instructions provided fail to provide guidance on the need for a secure mounting.

It is easy to overlook on the installation instructions the correct routing of the rope used for lifting. There is a hole in the cam lock fitting through which the cord should be threaded. Unfortunately the hole is barely large enough for the provided rope, which would make it difficult to upsize the rope.

Which brings me to the issue of the gaps between pulley cheeks and the sheaves. The gap is enough that the provided rope can jump out of the sheave groove and become wedged. The sheaves are designed so that squeezing the cheeks to reduce the gap results in friction at the axle before the gap is significantly reduced. While a larger rope could eliminate the risk of jamming, the hole in the cam lock does not permit such a substitution. It is for this reason, and the potential that a person could be misled by the plastic sheetrock anchors and fail to attach to solid wood, that I am giving 4 stars rather than 5.

Additional comments -- As others mention, the hooks to hang the bike do not really have enough curve to hold securely and you probably will need to do some bending to get a good result. My seat does not have a structure to which the hooks would attach, so I use a cord under a frame section and secure the hooks to that. If you have a speedometer or the like mounted on handle bars there is a possibility of conflict with hooks, and you may need to be careful to avoid damage to any wire connecting to a sensor. The cleat provided to tie off the rope when the bike is lifted is definitely pretty cheesy, but the cam lock is good enough that the cleat is really not needed. If you are a belt and suspenders person you might want to upgrade the cleat. Otherwise the cleat basically just provides a method to get excess rope out of the way.

So while this is not perfect, it provides a good solution at a good price, and I would buy another one if I had a second bike.
text_fidelity_b: Bike Hoist Bicycle Lift for Garage Ceiling Storage, Heavy Duty Mountain Bicycle Hanging Rack with 3 Pulley and 45 ft Adjustable Rope | 100 lb Capacity

WOD Nation Knee Sleeves for Weightlifting (1 Pair) Premium Support & Compression - Powerlifting & Weight Lifting - 5mm Neoprene Sleeve for The Best Squats - Fits Both Women & Men Let's start with the sleeves:

I am a wedding photographer with two bad knees and I needed a pair of sleeves that could provide good support and be comfortable simultaneously. After reading many reviews, I eventually bought these because of the ranking and many reviews.
The sleeves fitted tight with very good compression over my knee, but at the both ends they were so uncomfortable. There is a lot of pressure in both ends that were biting my skin and would left a considerable mark after I took them off after a while. But I got used to it after a 15 minutes.
Therefore I gave them a test (actually twice in two days). I used them outdoors for around four hours with very mild activity (walking sitting, going indoors, etc.), in a day that was warm but not hot or humid. When I took them off after I came back, they almost burnt backs of my knees, because they trapped all the sweat and they were entirely wet on that area. And my knees were itching for an hour too! So they didn't leave me any other choice rather than calling the customer service to use their 100% satisfaction money back guarantee. Here is what happened then:

I messaged the customer service, and the only respond I received was that "Amazon handles our returns, and you just go there and return the items". Ok, if you are an Amazon user you know that Amazon accepts returns on almost anything this way, it is not satisfaction guarantee. So I returned the used pairs (means you have to pack them again, print the label and drop them off if you are not satisfied). I would never use those pairs anyways, but just saying this is not satisfaction guarantee. I am sure that the returned pairs should go to trash can when they receive them. Satisfaction guarantee means you are not satisfied: money back! Just sayin'.

All in all, I ordered two of "Ultra Flex Athletics Knee Compression Sleeve"s , and they were just the perfect match. They are kind of fabric and they breathe and are super comfortable even for long uses like mine.
text_fidelity_b: WOD Nation Knee Sleeves for Weightlifting (1 Pair) Premium Support & Compression - Powerlifting & Weight Lifting - 5mm Neoprene Sleeve for The Best Squats - Fits Both Women & Men

Over the years, we have owned all different brands of basketballs, but we always come back to the better quality of Spalding.

text_fidelity_a: RaceWax Ski P-tex Base Repair Kit: 10 ptex, Metal Scraper, 3 3M Buffing Pads Got this to do some repair work on my 30 something year old xc skis.  Worked great and so easy to do.  I had some pretty bad gouges and scraps from skiing on frozen gravel.  Spent a bit of time preping the bases by removing the wax base and cleaning up the edges of the gouges.  I also used my waxing iron to preheat the bases.  Lit the candle and moved slowly and carefully.  Keep the candle close to your work and hold it at an angle to keep the carbon to a minimum.  After cooling down the included scraper mad quick work of leveling out the area.  A couple quick passes with the scotch brite pads and a finally buff with the white pad and I was ready for a base wax.  I have only been out once since the repair (figures all the snow melted) but the repair held perfectly.  I used about a third of a candle to repair about 4 ft. of scratches of at least a fingernail width wide.  So much cheaper than a new pair of skis.
text_fidelity_b: RaceWax Ski P-tex Base Repair Kit: 10 ptex, Metal Scraper, 3 3M Buffing Pads

text_fidelity_a:
Fox Outdoor Products Mission Ready Drop Leg Holster I wanted to try a drop leg holster for some time and came across this model in desert camo through another vendor. For the price, and because I had heard good things about Fox, I decided to take advantage of the reduced price and see how good (or bad) this holster really is.

The first day, after strapping it on and making all the adjustments I could, I carried around a mini ball peen hammer just to try to get used to it. Why did I choose a hammer? While I am CCW licensed, Florida does not currently allow "open carry". So I had to put something of measurable weight in the holster without alarming the neighbors or anyone driving by on our street. I could imagine someone seeing me with a drop leg holster and calling our local law enforcement, not knowing that their was no gun in the holster -- but assuming there was.Yes, the weight of the hammer head made the holster cant backwards, so I switched to a rubber mallet. This provided a much better balance.

Then I switched to a Glock 23 and a Springfield XD-45 MOD 2 and alternately carried both around inside our home, After trying my darndest to get it to fit properly, I came to the following conclusions:

1. This is a cool looking and well constructed rig. The desert camo design is well done, the material is light and flexible, and the various
clips, belts and fasteners work like they should.
2 The holster accommodated both the Springfield and Glock perfectly and the strap easily fastened over the gun butt.
3. It is very light and designed to fit comfortably against your thigh.
4. And of course it easily carries a lighter weight weapon like a Kahr PM9 and a Glock 42. In fact the smaller and lighter pistols eliminate
the bounding around explained below. But who wants to carry a "pocket pistol" in a drop leg holster?

But, and this is a "big but" for me, the single strap that fastens the holster around your thigh just couldn't keep the holster secure and steady. It bounced while walking and really moved around when running (even at my slow pace). I tightened the thigh strap so that over 14" of strap was outside the buckle, but it just never felt secure. No one wants that feeling -- you want your gun to be right where it's supposed to be -- all of the time.

This holster really needs two improvements: 1. It needs a second strap to go around the thigh, one high and one low. 2. It also needs more vertical adjustment so that it can be carried a bit higher on your belt. Both of these changes would result in a better fit and should eliminate excess movement.
text_fidelity_b: Fox Outdoor Products Mission Ready Drop Leg Holster
